description: A sentence that denies one framing only to assert another ("it's not X, it's Y"; "this isn't about A, it's about B"), where nobody had claimed X.
instead: State Y directly. Keep the contrast only when a reader actually holds X, and then name who holds it and why.

description: Items grouped in threes by habit (three adjectives, three parallel clauses, three examples) where the material has two or four.
instead: Count what the material really has and list that many. If one item is the strongest, give it alone.

description: An opening that warms up instead of starting: a remark on how much the topic matters, how fast things change, or how many people get it wrong.
instead: Cut to the first sentence that says something only this post says, and start there.

description: A final paragraph that restates what the post just said ("in short", "ultimately", "at the end of the day") without adding anything.
instead: End on the last new thing: the consequence, the next step, or the opening image seen again in a new light.

description: A post or section that opens with a question the writer answers at once ("Ever wondered why...? Here's why.").
instead: Open with the answer, or with the fact that makes the question worth asking.

description: Runs of one-line paragraphs or very short sentences used for drama, more often than the writer's own work uses them.
instead: Join the lines into the paragraph they belong to. Keep a short line only where the writer's own pieces would, for a real turn.

description: Grand or abstract words where a plain one fits ("landscape", "realm", "tapestry", "delve", "leverage", "robust", "seamless").
instead: Ask what the thing concretely is or does, and say that in the word the writer would use out loud.

description: Details that sound exact but come from nowhere: round invented percentages, unnamed studies, a person or company that is not in the material.
instead: Use a figure or case from the material with its source, or say plainly that it is not known. Never fill the slot with an invented one.

description: Em dashes used far more often than the writer's own pieces use them, for asides that commas, parentheses or a new sentence would carry.
instead: Keep the writer's own rate. Past it, make the aside its own sentence or fold it in with a comma.

description: Sentences that announce what comes next or what matters ("here's the thing", "let's break it down", "it's worth noting") instead of saying it.
instead: Delete the announcement and let the next sentence do the work it promised.

description: Words that claim importance without showing it ("crucial", "game-changing", "incredibly", "truly", "powerful").
instead: Replace the intensifier with the fact that would make a reader feel it is important, or drop it.

description: A reflexive "of course, it depends" or "there are pros and cons" that balances a claim the post has every reason to make.
instead: Commit to the claim the evidence supports. Name a limit only when there is a real case where the claim fails, and give the case.
